content.text: The data clearly shows a step-change pattern: before July 2018, the core zone's sensor was tracking closely with the other zones (monthly means differed by less than 1°C, and it was even cooler than the perimeter during daytime hours); after July 2018, the core's sensor shows a near-constant ~25.1°C monthly mean, with the seasonality almost entirely lost, and is warmer than every other zone in every month including the winter (in December, core is 25.1°C vs 22.4°C in the neighboring zone, with an hourly deviation of 0.3–2.6°C positive in all time slots). This abrupt ~2°C step, the decoupling from the seasonal variation that all the other sensors continue to show, and the fact that its setpoint hasn't changed all point to an offset/drift in a single sensor, not to a change in physical load (in which case, we should still see a seasonal variation and diurnal response like the other zones).
